title: Clients see the staff SSID but cannot establish service
scenario: Staff clients are configured for WPA2-Personal/AES on CCNA-Lab, with the issued lab passphrase StudyLab-2026!. They can see the SSID but cannot establish a working connection. The site has no external RADIUS server or local EAP configuration. The following are representative records.

exhibits.title: AireOS WLAN 2 security
exhibits.text:
Profile: CCNA-USERS; SSID: CCNA-Lab; enabled
WPA: disabled; WPA2: enabled
AES: enabled; TKIP: disabled
AKM 802.1X: enabled; PSK: disabled

exhibits.title: Authentication services
exhibits.text:
External RADIUS authentication servers: none
Local EAP: disabled

exhibits.title: Client profile
exhibits.text:
SSID: CCNA-Lab
Authentication: WPA2-Personal
Encryption: AES
Shared-key profile configured

question: Which configuration mismatch is established by these records?
options: The WLAN selected a different cipher from the clients' saved AES setting
The WLAN expects 802.1X while clients expect a Personal PSK
The client and controller chose different SSID names
The controller is waiting for an address after security completion
explanation: The WLAN explicitly has 802.1X enabled and PSK disabled while the clients expect Personal key management. WPA2/AES is already correct. The record supports this mismatch without needing to infer an unshown exclusion event or exact handshake failure.
fix:
In the authorized lab's AireOS-style GUI, disable WLAN 2 while editing. Open Security → Layer 2, disable 802.1X AKM, enable PSK, set ASCII key StudyLab-2026!, retain WPA2/AES with WPA/TKIP off, Apply, then enable the WLAN and Save Configuration. If a client is actually shown excluded, handle only that client's remaining exclusion using the platform's supported procedure.

Start a fresh connection. Verify security/admitted state, intended VLAN/address/gateway and traffic to a known server. Do not conclude that a saved PSK field alone proves recovery.

title: New wireless clients cannot obtain their intended addresses
scenario: A centrally switched AireOS WLAN moved users to dynamic interface users in VLAN 10. Controller management uses tagged VLAN 99. DHCP proxy is explicitly disabled in this scenario, so client DHCP is bridged into VLAN 10. R1's 10.0.10.0/24 scope and gateway 10.0.10.1 work for a wired test client. The following are representative diagnostics.

exhibits.title: WLC current client and interface review
exhibits.text:
Current client security event: WPA2 key establishment completed
Client state: DHCP_REQD; current IP: Unknown
WLAN interface users: VLAN 10, 10.0.10.2/24
DHCP proxy: disabled; bridging DHCP to client VLAN
Fresh wireless client requests observed; no lease

exhibits.title: SW1 controller-facing trunk
exhibits.text:
Port: Fa0/24; status trunking; native VLAN 1
VLANs allowed: 99
VLANs allowed and active: 99
VLANs forwarding: 99

exhibits.title: Wired validation
exhibits.text:
VLAN 10 exists and forwards on the R1 uplink
Wired VLAN 10 test client receives 10.0.10.101/24
Wired test reaches 10.0.10.1 and the known test server

question: Which failure is directly supported?
options: The WLAN's mapped VLAN lacks DHCP service even for wired clients
The client stopped before WPA2 key establishment completed
The WLC uplink omits the required client VLAN
The AP lost its management registration before client requests began
explanation: Security has completed, but the central client VLAN is absent from the controller uplink's allowed list. In the explicitly stated DHCP-bridging design, VLAN 10's requests and replies cannot cross that link. The successful wired test establishes that the separate VLAN 10 service path exists.
fix:
On the lab switch add the client VLAN without removing management:

```ios
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/24
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces trunk
```

Confirm 10,99 are allowed/active/forwarding. Have the wireless client request a fresh lease, then verify its 10.0.10.x/24 address, gateway and server access. Retest controller management. A different DHCP-proxy design requires following that design's server/interface path instead of assuming every request remains an unchanged broadcast.
